name: VibeInbox for Elementor
author: VibeInbox / Erez Ben Shoham

sections.description:
VibeInbox for Elementor connects your Elementor Pro forms to VibeInbox, an email marketing service. Every submission becomes a signup in the VibeInbox form you choose: the contact joins that form’s lists and receives its welcome email.

  • No code, no URLs to copy. Add “VibeInbox” under the form’s Actions After Submit and pick the VibeInbox form from a list.
  • Field mapping in each field. Email and phone are found by field type. For the name, choose “Full name” (or “First name” / “Last name”) in the field’s “VibeInbox field” setting.
  • Consent stays honest. If the form has a consent checkbox (an Acceptance field), it decides: signups who leave it unticked are saved without marketing consent. A form without a consent checkbox counts every signup as consent — say so on the form.
  • A visitor’s signup never fails because of us. If VibeInbox does not answer, the visitor still sees the form’s success message; the failure is recorded on the settings page. Keep Elementor’s “Collect Submissions” action on, and the signup is also kept in WordPress.
  • Every form on your site in one list. Settings → VibeInbox lists every Elementor form in pages, posts, popups and templates, shows which ones send to VibeInbox and what else they still do, with a link to edit each one.

Requirements

  • Elementor Pro 3.5 or newer (the Form widget is part of Elementor Pro).
  • A VibeInbox account and an API key (VibeControl → API).

External services

This plugin connects your site to VibeInbox, an email marketing service operated by Q.C.M Computing Services Ltd (Israel). It sends data only as described here.

  • When a visitor submits a form that has the “VibeInbox” action: the form’s fields as the visitor filled them (for example name, email, phone, consent checkbox and any other fields), the form’s ID and name, the page address, the visitor’s browser identifier (user agent) and IP address are sent to https://www.vibecontrol.co.il/api/forms/<form>/elementor, the VibeInbox form you chose. Fields set to “Don’t send” are not sent.
  • When you open the plugin’s settings page or the Elementor editor: the plugin asks https://api.vibeinbox.app/api/v1/forms for the list of your VibeInbox forms, sending your API key. No visitor data is sent in this request.

Nothing is sent when no VibeInbox action is set on a form.

  • Service: https://vibeinbox.app/
  • Terms of use: https://vibeinbox.app/terms
  • Privacy policy: https://vibeinbox.app/privacy
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate the plugin (Plugins → Add New → search “VibeInbox for Elementor”, or upload the zip).
  2. Go to Settings → VibeInbox, paste your API key from VibeControl → API, save, and press “Test connection”.
  3. Edit a form in Elementor: under Actions After Submit add “VibeInbox”, and in the VibeInbox section choose the VibeInbox form.
  4. In the name field, set “VibeInbox field” to “Full name”. Save, and send a test signup.
sections.faq:
Where do I choose the mailing list?

In VibeInbox. Each VibeInbox form decides its lists, welcome email and thank-you settings; in Elementor you choose the form. To send different Elementor forms to different lists, create a VibeInbox form for each.

I already send my forms to another service. Can I switch gradually?

Yes. Elementor runs every action in the list, so you can add VibeInbox next to the existing action, check that signups arrive, and then remove the old one. Settings → VibeInbox shows which forms still use other actions.

Does it work with the free version of Elementor?

No. The Form widget is part of Elementor Pro.

What happens if a submission fails?

The visitor sees the normal success message. The failure (time, form, reason) is shown under Settings → VibeInbox. With “Collect Submissions” on, the signup is also in Elementor → Submissions.
